At that time, Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit, and she exclaimed in a loud voice and said: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And how has this fallen to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, as soon as the voice of your greeting sounded in my ears, the infant in my womb leaped with joy. And blessed are you who have believed, because the things that were spoken to you by the Lord will be fulfilled. And Mary said: My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior, for He has regarded the lowliness of His handmaid; behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed. For He who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is His name, and His mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear Him.

Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in keeping with His great mercy has given us rebirth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, into an inheritance incorruptible and undefiled and unfading, preserved in heaven for you, who in the power of God are kept safe through faith for salvation, prepared to be revealed at the last time. Dearly beloved: Do not be astonished if the world hates you. We ourselves know that we have been brought over from death to life, since we love the brethren. Whoever does not love remains in death. Anyone who hates his brother is a murderer. You know, too, that no murderer has eternal life remaining in himself. By this we know the love of God: He laid down His life for us, and we must lay down our lives for the brethren. Whoever has this world’s goods, and sees that his brother is in need, and shuts off his compassion from him, how does the love of God remain in him? My little children, let us not love with words, nor with our tongues, but in action and in truth.

At that time, Jesus told this parable to the Pharisees: A certain man held a great supper and invited many. And at the hour of the supper he sent his servant to tell the invited guests to come, because all is now ready. And all of them together began to make excuses. The first said to him: I bought a farm, and I have need to go out and see it; I beg you, hold me excused. And a second said: I bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to test them; I beg you, hold me excused. And another said: I have taken a wife, and for that reason I cannot come. And on his return the servant told his master these things. Then the householder, in anger, said to his servant: Go out quickly into the squares and streets of the city, and bring the poor and the infirm and the blind and the lame in here. And the servant said: Master, it has been done as you commanded, and there is still room. And the master said to the servant: Go out into the roads and hedges, and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled. But I say to you that none of those men who were invited will taste my supper.

At that time, publicans and sinners were coming near to Jesus to hear Him. And the Pharisees and scribes were grumbling, saying: This man receives sinners and eats with them. And He spoke this parable to them, saying: What man among you who has a hundred sheep, if he has lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that had been lost, until he finds it? And when he has found it, he places it on his shoulders, rejoicing; and when he comes home, he calls his friends and neighbors together, saying to them: Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that had been lost. I say to you that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner doing penance than over ninety-nine just persons who do not need penance. Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she has lost one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep out the house and seek diligently until she finds it? And when she has found it, she calls her friends and neighbors together, saying: Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma which I had lost. Thus I say to you, there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner doing penance.

For creation has been subjected to emptiness, not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it in hope; for creation itself too will be set free from the slavery of corruption into the liberty of the glory of God’s sons. At that time, when the crowds were thronging Jesus to hear the word of God, He Himself was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret. And He saw two boats standing beside the lake; but the fishermen had disembarked and were washing the nets. And going aboard one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, He asked him to pull back a little from the shore. And sitting down, He was teaching the crowds out of the boat. And when He had stopped speaking, He said to Simon: Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch. And in answer Simon said to Him: Master, we toiled through the whole night and caught nothing; yet at Your word I will let down the net. And having done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their net began to tear. And they signaled to their partners in the other boat that they should come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they were almost sinking. Seeing this, Simon Peter fell down at the knees of Jesus, saying: Go away from me, because I am a sinful man, Lord. For astonishment had seized him and all who were with him at the haul of fish which they had taken; and likewise James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners. And Jesus said to Simon: Have no fear; from now on you will be catching men. And when they had drawn their boats up on land, they left everything and followed Him.

At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: Unless your justice abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter into the kingdom of heaven. You have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not kill; and whoever kills will be subject to judgment. But I say to you that whoever is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. And he who says to his brother, Raca, will be subject to the council. And he who says, Fool, will be subject to the Gehenna of fire. If, therefore, you offer your gift at the altar, and there you remember that your brother has something against you, leave there your gift before the altar, and go first and be reconciled with your brother; and then you shall come and offer your gift.

Brethren: I speak in human terms, on account of the infirmity of your flesh. For just as you presented your members to serve uncleanness and iniquity, leading to iniquity, so now present your members to serve justice, leading to sanctification. But now, freed from sin and made God’s slaves, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and as its end, eternal life. For the wages of sin, death; but the grace of God, eternal life, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

At that time, Jesus addressed His disciples with this parable: There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and the steward was reported to him as having squandered his goods. So he summoned him and said to him: What is this that I hear of you? Give an account of your stewardship, since you can no longer be steward. And the steward said to himself: What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my stewardship? To dig I am not strong enough; to beg I am ashamed. I know what I will do, so that, once I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses. So he called in his master’s debtors one by one, and said to the first: How much do you owe my master? He replied: A hundred jars of oil. And he told him: Take your note; sit down at once and write fifty. Next he said to another: And you, how much do you owe? He said: A hundred cors of wheat. He told him: Take your bond and write eighty. And the master commended the unjust steward because he had acted wisely; for the children of this world are wiser than the children of light in their own generation. And I say to you, make yourselves friends by means of the unjust mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the everlasting dwellings.
